meta.title: What wins, what loses
meta.question: Which behaviours win accounts and which lose them?
caveats: Effective = coded + in a best account (Q22, Q24); ineffective = coded − in a worst account (Q23, Q25).
Class (Johnston 1995 rule, adapted): of ≥ 10 experiential mentions, ≥ 2/3 ineffective = dissatisfier; ≥ 2/3 effective = satisfier; ≥ 1/4 each = critical; else neutral.
Codes are one coder's, checked blind on 200 answers (behaviour alpha 0.87).

behaviours.label: Knows my business
behaviours.definition: The salesperson or vendor understands the decision-maker's business, industry, company or needs. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Responsive
behaviours.definition: Replies and acts promptly; available when needed. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Continuity and long relationship
behaviours.definition: A relationship built over time with the same people; − : turnover, inconsistency, no relationship. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Solves my problem
behaviours.definition: Helps the decision-maker solve a problem or reach a result; consultative. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Knows the product
behaviours.definition: Knowledge of their own products, services or technology. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Brings insight and ideas
behaviours.definition: Brings new ideas, innovation, strategic perspective or the big picture. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Brings the vendor's organisation
behaviours.definition: Can mobilise the vendor's own people, specialists and resources for the customer. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Committed to us
behaviours.definition: Gives the customer priority, time and effort. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Partners with us
behaviours.definition: Works with the customer as a partner, not a seller. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Price and value for money
behaviours.definition: Price, cost, or value for money. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Product quality
behaviours.definition: Quality or performance of what is sold. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Competent people
behaviours.definition: The people are capable at their job (general competence). Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Fits our environment
behaviours.definition: The offering fits or integrates with the customer's environment and needs. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Keeps promises; delivers
behaviours.definition: Delivers what was promised; keeps commitments; what is delivered matches what was sold. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Empowered to decide
behaviours.definition: Has the authority to make decisions or commitments. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Personal attention
behaviours.definition: Personal, human attention and rapport. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Flexible
behaviours.definition: Adapts offering, terms or approach to the customer. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: A stable, established vendor
behaviours.definition: The vendor is established and likely to be around; − : company status questionable. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Support after the sale
behaviours.definition: Service and support when the product is in use. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Puts my needs before their sale
behaviours.definition: Serves the decision-maker's interest rather than the vendor's sale; − : pushy, oversells, only wants the sale. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Prepared
behaviours.definition: Comes prepared to the meeting. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Communicates clearly
behaviours.definition: Clear, relevant communication. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Professional
behaviours.definition: Professional conduct and image. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Proven track record
behaviours.definition: Evidence of past success: experience, references, a record on similar problems. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Honest and trustworthy
behaviours.definition: Honest, transparent, keeps their word; can be trusted. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Listens
behaviours.definition: Listens to what the decision-maker wants rather than talking. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Easy to deal with
behaviours.definition: Simple and efficient to work with; − : complex, cumbersome, hard to pin down, badly organised. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Quantifies the value
behaviours.definition: Shows the return on investment or quantified impact. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Treats me with respect
behaviours.definition: Treats the decision-maker as competent; not arrogant or condescending. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly

behaviours.label: Helps me sell it internally
behaviours.definition: Helps the decision-maker carry the idea inside their own company. Polarity: + experienced well, − badly
